entities.summary: Finland is a sovereign nation in Northern Europe, Europe. Its capital is Helsinki. Official languages include Finnish, Swedish. Government: Unitary parliamentary republic. Population: approximately 5.6 million. Area: 338,455 km². Comprehensive index for Finland covering Finno-Ugric settlement, Swedish rule (~650 years, 1150s-1809), Northern Crusades, Swedish-Russian confrontations, Russian Grand Duchy (1809-1917, autonomous), Finnish national awakening (Kalevala 1835, Snellman, language movement), independence 1917, Civil War 1918 (Whites vs Reds), Winter War 1939-40 (Soviet invasion, heroic defence, sisu), Continuation War 1941-44, Finlandization (Cold War Soviet influence), welfare state, EU accession 1995, NATO accession 2023 (triggered by Russia's Ukraine invasion).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Finland's struggle for independence and its heroic defense against Soviet invasion in the Winter War had significant regional implications, influencing the course of European politics during World War II. The country's post-war path to EU accession and NATO membership has also shaped its position as a key player in Northern Europe.
